memory_update.text: VECO should remain a priority underfollowed equipment candidate for the CPO/silicon-photonics manufacturing-stack node because it has direct 2026 evidence of large InP laser manufacturing equipment orders tied to silicon photonics.
FORM should be tracked as a wafer-level optical/electrical test bottleneck candidate; evidence is strong at the product/partnership level, but later layers must verify material revenue exposure.

AXTI is a rare public InP substrate exposure and fits the underfollowed materials lens, but survival into later layers depends on export-control permits, customer concentration, revenue mix, and margin proof.

Non-US-listed chokepoint names such as Aixtron, Oxford Instruments, Huber+Suhner, and Advantest appear relevant to MOCVD/etch/connectivity/test but were not included because this pass requested US-listed companies; they should be retained as private/non-US reference context in later mapping.

node: CPO and silicon-photonics upstream manufacturing stack: InP substrates, epitaxy, MOCVD, etch/deposition, bonding, optical test
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the US-listed universe around scarce upstream CPO/silicon-photonics manufacturing inputs. The strongest underfollowed chokepoint candidates are Veeco for InP laser manufacturing equipment, FormFactor for wafer-level silicon-photonics/CPO test automation, and AXT for InP substrates. Teradyne is included as a higher-attention reference because its Photon 100 product directly targets high-volume silicon-photonics and CPO test, but its company-level exposure is less pure due to broader automated test and robotics businesses.
